HTML Email Signatures

Besnik Qunaku · Software Developer

Hand-coded, table-based email signatures. No generator, no framework, no web fonts, no @font-face. Written against the constraints of the clients they have to survive — principally Outlook Classic, which renders through Microsoft Word rather than a browser engine.

Personal

Signatures for my own correspondence. No logo, so identity is carried by a typographic monogram set in Georgia — live text in a coloured table cell, not an image, so it survives with images disabled.

Compatibility & testing

Stated plainly, because an untested claim is worth less than an honest gap.

ClientEngineStatus
Gmail — web (macOS)BlinkTested
Gmail — iOS / Android appWebKit / BlinkTested
Apple Mail — macOSWebKitTested
Outlook New / Outlook.comWebView2 / BlinkTested
Outlook Classic — WindowsMicrosoft WordNot tested — no Windows machine
On Outlook Classic. I work on macOS and do not currently have a Windows machine, so I have not verified these signatures in Outlook Classic and I am not going to claim otherwise. Outlook for Mac is not a substitute: it renders through WebKit, so passing there would be no evidence at all about the Word engine. What I have done instead is write the markup against the Word engine's documented constraints from the outset — the table below is the specific list I coded against. Given a Windows machine or a Litmus/Email on Acid account, I can verify and correct any remaining issues quickly, because I know where they come from.

Outlook Classic constraints these signatures are built around

ConstraintConsequenceHow it is handled here
No flexbox, grid or floatModern layout collapsesNested tables only, role="presentation"
margin is unreliableSpacing drifts or vanishesCell padding and explicit spacer rows
CSS borders dropped inconsistentlyRules and dividers disappearRules are bgcolor table cells of fixed height
line-height reinterpretedText sits too tall or too tightmso-line-height-rule:exactly on every text cell
Phantom spacing around tablesUnexplained gapsmso-table-lspace/rspace:0pt, border-collapse:collapse
No @font-faceWeb fonts silently fall backWeb-safe stacks; brand font declared first for machines that have it
No data: URIsEmbedded images do not renderIcon served from an absolute https URL
Images blocked by defaultLogo becomes an empty boxWordmark and monogram are live text; icon carries alt plus a text link
background-image needs VMLBackgrounds drop outSolid bgcolor only — no background images used
No border-radiusRounded corners square offGeometry is square by design, so nothing is lost
max-width ignoredLayout overflowsWidths as HTML attributes and CSS, integers only
Link colour forced blueBrand colour overridden<a> and an inner <span> both styled

Gmail also clips messages over roughly 102 KB. The largest signature here is under 7 KB, so nothing is at risk of truncation.

Installing

The copy buttons above copy the rendered signature, not its source — which is what every signature editor expects.

Gmail

  1. Click Copy signature on the variant you want.
  2. Settings → See all settings → General → Signature → Create new.
  3. Paste with Cmd/Ctrl+V. Not “paste as plain text”.
  4. Tick “Insert this signature before quoted text… and remove the ‘--’ line”.
  5. Set both Signature defaults dropdowns, then Save Changes.

Outlook New / Web

  1. Settings → Mail → Compose and reply.
  2. Paste, tick both new-message and reply options, Save.

Outlook Classic

  1. File → Options → Mail → Signatures… → New.
  2. Paste, assign to new messages and replies, OK.
